subject: RFP: Stratus Financial — proforma token schedule & billing playbook
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <procurement@stratusfinancial.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@stratusfinancial.com>, Samir Patel <itsecurity@stratusfinancial.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RFP commercial questions — token pricing, commits, overages

Hi Elliot,

Thanks for the initial RFP submission. Procurement and IT Security reviewed the commercial appendix and we had a few high-priority clarifications before we advance to procurement redlines:

- Can you provide a concrete invoice example showing 3 months of ramp, a 6M annual commit, and how overages would be charged (per-token vs monthly true-up)?
- How do you provide credits for sustained underconsumption each quarter? Is there an automatic rollover?
- We need explicit language on burst capacity — what are the rates and how are they capped?
- Any standard discounts for multi-year commitments or prepay? Please include the math (effective $/1k tokens).

Samir also asked for confirmation that hosting logs used for billing are auditable and that invoice inputs can be reconciled to your Console exports (we'll follow up with a security questionnaire separately).

Can you get us a short proforma and an annotated example invoice by next Wednesday? We want to show this to Finance.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager
Stratus Financial

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Chen <procurement@stratusfinancial.com>
Cc: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@stratusfinancial.com>, Samir Patel <itsecurity@stratusfinancial.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: RFP commercial questions — token pricing, commits, overages

Olivia —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is a short proforma (Stratus_Pricing_Proforma_v1.xlsx) plus an annotated PDF with the same worked examples. Highlights up front:

- Invoice example: sheet "InvoiceExamples" shows a 6M-token annual commit, with monthly drawdown. We show a 3-month ramp (25% / 50% / 75%) then steady state. Overage billing is monthly and charged at the overage rate in the ratecard; we also offer a monthly true-up option where overages are credited toward the following month up to a cushion.
- Underconsumption credits: we provide a quarterly reconciliation. Any shortfall against the pro-rated commit is eligible for a credit ladder (see row 42 of the proforma). Credits do not automatically roll beyond the contract year unless a renewal with rollover is agreed.
- Burst capacity: two modes — "On-demand burst" billed at 2.0x the negotiated per-token rate (subject to a per-month cap), or "Reserved burst" (pre-purchased burst buckets) priced at a discounted multiplier. Both options and caps are in the "BurstOptions" tab.
- Multi-year / prepay discounts: table on "Discounts" tab shows tiered effective $/1k tokens for 1-, 2-, and 3-year commitments and for prepay vs monthly invoicing. Example: 2-year, 10% prepay yields ~0.88x on the base per-token price (example math is in the sheet).

Samir — regarding auditability: our Console exports provide token-level usage CSVs (timestamped, model id, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_id). We can provide a short reconciliation guide and a sample export for your auditing team. We also support signed S3 delivery of invoice inputs for customers that require immutable archives.

Next steps: Marissa (cc'd) manages commercial modeling for enterprise deals — we'll follow up with a redline-friendly proforma that includes two commercial structures (Commit-first with burst buckets vs. Smoothing/true-up model) and an invoice worked example for each. We'll target delivery by Wed 26 May.

Regards,
Elliot Price
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
E: elliot.price@redwoodinference.com | M: +1-415-555-0192

On Wed, May 26, 2027 at 08:12 AM Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Jordan —
>
> Attached is the initial proforma; we'll send the redline-friendly version shortly.

Thanks Elliot — couple quick clarifications from Finance after reviewing the example invoice:

1) In your invoice example the overage rate is shown as a flat per-token charge. Can you confirm whether overage tokens are calculated before or after any applied discounts (i.e., do overage tokens get the same volume discount as committed tokens within the same billing period)?
2) For the quarterly reconciliation credit, is the credit applied as a reduction on the next invoice or issued as a one-time credit memo? Finance prefers a reduction on the next invoice to simplify cashflow.

If you can explicitly show the invoice math both ways (credit memo vs invoice reduction) that will help.

Thanks,
Jordan Mills
Manager, Strategic Sourcing
Stratus Financial

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@stratusfinancial.com>, Olivia Chen <procurement@stratusfinancial.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: RFP commercial questions — token pricing, commits, overages

Jordan / Olivia —

Thanks for the follow-ups — attached is a redlined proforma (PDF) and a second workbook that explicitly shows both invoice flows you requested. Short answers up front:

- Overage discounting: overage tokens are billed at the published overage rate (no automatic volume discount), but we offer a pooled true-up option where, if the customer opts in, monthly usage across the billing period is evaluated against tier thresholds and overage is credited as if it had received the tiered rate. This is an opt-in commercial concession and is implemented as an invoice reduction during the true-up cycle. Example: see "InvoiceExamples" tab, rows 110-132 which show the same charges with and without true-up.
- Credit application: by default credits are issued as an invoice reduction on the following invoice; we can issue a credit memo on request, but most customers prefer the invoice reduction approach (matches your Finance preference).
- Burst mechanics: the proforma now includes a capped monthly burst band (SLA ring-fence) and a separate reserved burst SKU. We included a worked example for a three-day traffic spike and the resulting capped charges.
- Pricing sensitivity: we added a one-page summary for Finance showing effective $/1k tokens under three scenarios (steady-state, ramp, and high-surprise month) for 1/2/3 year commitments.

Admin: I've attached the HubSpot deal link and a DocuSign envelope placeholder in the metadata. If Stratus is comfortable with the invoice flow and the capped burst construct, we'll prepare a final commercial term sheet for signature. Marissa will reach out to align on any final concession language.

Appended below is a short sample invoice excerpt (redacted) so you can drop it into your internal models — copy/paste friendly.

--- SAMPLE INVOICE EXCERPT (redacted) ---
Invoice month: 2027-06
Committed tokens (monthly pro-rate): 500,000
Actual tokens consumed: 720,000
Base per-token rate (commit tier): $0.0100 per token
Overage rate (published): $0.0150 per token
Overage tokens: 220,000
Overage charge: 220,000 * $0.0150 = $3,300.00
If true-up opted in and effective tier reduces overage to $0.0110: Credit applied = 220,000 * ($0.0150 - $0.0110) = $880.00 (applied as invoice reduction)

If this looks good we'll convert the proforma to a redline-ready term sheet and push for a signature cycle.

Best,
Elliot Price
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0192
